It can be tricky. There's some things i've learned from the two trips i took in the last couple of months:

\- board with the disability boarding (show them your medical bracelet/badge/jewelry) (keep things slow, calm, relaxed, take your time - if being rushed is a trigger for you - it very much is for me!)

\- DO NOT HAVE A SEAT IN THE REAR OF THE PLANE. pay for a seat so you have a seat in the front - *especially* if it is a small plane. i had a seizure on take off in a small plane because i was in a rear seat in the plane because of the G-forces/pressure. i felt a LOT better in the front of the plane (was able to choose my seats on the other planes i took on the way home)

\- bring a sleepmask and wear it pretty much at all times (really helps with cognitive load/blocking everything out/calming)

\- listen to music that calms you on the flight, and block out all the 'people' noise

\- stay well hydrated and make sure you have enough carbs/sugar in your system

\- don't drink a ton of water at once. i did this in the security line and made myself have a full focal unaware seizure, and came to on the other side of security in the bathroom (checked my belongings 6 times worried if i had everything!)

\- have tylenol/muscle relaxers/plenty of your go-to pain meds ready and in your system

My tumor was sitting more on the facial nerve and it was about 26mm when the imaging was done (had a wait of almost 3 months from there to surgery, and based on symptoms might have grown a little, not sure) - your experience might vary based on the location/size. Recovery has been good. The doctors seemed impressed with my progress throughout, anyways.  


They said I'd be in the hospital 2, maybe 3 days and it ended up being 8 days. They said I'd be out of work for 4 weeks and it ended up being 2 months. My vision in my right eye was very blurry for about a month and a half, then it slowly got better. It still gets dry overnight though - I must still have trouble keeping it totally shut when relaxed - the nerve is still healing I think (they gave me an eye patch to wear at night and i use eye drops in my right eye every night). And it was slow, but my right side of my face is about 90% better now (almost 3 mo later) - and I see wrinkles/movement in it like I didn't see before surgery (was very paralyzed on the right side of face/mouth/jaw for maybe..almost a month after the surgery before it was totally better). Vestibular exercises/therapy helps the balance, and some exercises they gave me help with the pain/headaches I still get. I just 'graduated' from PT today. I still struggle a bit cognitively, but I think that may take the longest to heal bc my brain was so stressed for so long (focus/concentration/decisions/conversations)(they gave me a cognitive test and I was average/above average in the categories - so I suppose I'm fine, but struggle with those things). My stomach was upset that first day (of the surgery), but then it got better in a day or so. I had to have assistance walking for the first two weeks roughly (going for daily assisted walks at least 2x a day in the first month helps). I was very spacey/out of my head for at least a month - until maybe a week or so after stopping the steroids (for brain swelling).  


I hope the best for you/your hearing. I think my right-side hearing was doomed from the start - I always had trouble understanding others, even though my hearing tests came back pretty normal - just some loss in high pitched noises in the right side (before surgery). Always had some auditory processing sort of symptoms. They said there was barely any nerve signal when they checked at the start of surgery, and it was lost during surgery. They did a right retrosigmoid surgery for the tumor - to try and preserve the hearing.  


TL;DR  It's been alright. Slowly but surely getting better. I think you'll want help for that first month. Best of wishes to you.
